decisions: The filed hypothesis -- 'the override may change the operation without extending the original return-terminated worklist' -- is REFUTED. `print raw` under the single override shows `Basic Block 0 0x00401757-0x00401785`: flow resumed at 0x401770, the pushed continuation, and ran on to 0x401785. The continuation is retained.

The real gap: 0x401785 is another link of the same `push <cont>; push <target>; ret` idiom, still classified a return, so the 22-link body behind it is dead. Two overrides in one command already produced `GetProcAddress(LoadLibraryA(s_40151e),s_40152b)` on the unpatched tree -- nothing walked the chain, and nothing in the output said the next link existed.

Fixed at the driver tier (kuna-console), not the engine: the change only plants overrides the caller could have written by hand, so it needs no phases.toml option and cannot move any run that does not pass a `flow ... call` directive. This also kept it clear of the kuna-decomp / phases.toml / catalog-counter leases held by a concurrent builder.

Link test is `the run reaching this ret stored this ret's own fall-through address`. A real `call` also pushes its own fall-through, so a call instruction's literals are dropped; an ordinary epilogue never pushes the address after itself. Both are why the extension is safe to do unasked.

Literals are tracked per varnode within the instruction: SLEIGH's `push` macros are `tmp:4 = imm32; mysave:4 = tmp; *:4 ESP = mysave`, so the STORE value operand is a unique, never the constant. Reading the STORE operand alone found zero links.

The acceptance probe was UNRUNNABLE as filed (no target block). Bound to the dataset witness (binary_source dataset, sha verified byte-identical to the arena copy) and promoted onto a vendored reduction instead, because `--promote` refuses a dataset source and CI has no dataset.

measured.witness_after: 22 links recovered: GetProcAddress(LoadLibraryA()), MessageBoxA, ExitProcess, GetModuleHandleA, VirtualProtect, CreateFileA, VirtualAlloc, SetFilePointer, ReadFile x3, CloseHandle, three decrypt loops, GetForegroundWindow, GetWindowThreadProcessId, OpenProcess, ReadProcessMemory x2
measured.known_remaining: Stack arguments across the recovered links are still modelled as frame stores (`v15 = s_40151e;` beside `LoadLibraryA()`), so some call sites lose their argument list. That is the separate argument-recovery weakness the tester also reported (`calleearity`, `varargstackargs` did not help); it is not made worse here -- before the fix those call sites did not exist at all.
